key_insight: β-TeO3 is predicted from first principles to be a wide-gap n-type semiconductor with exceptionally high work functions, reaching about 8 eV.
engineering_relevance: This makes β-TeO3 a strong candidate for hole-transport, hole-injection, and transparent-electrode layers in optoelectronic devices such as solar cells and LEDs.
method: First-principles defect calculations for point impurities and vacancies
Work-function evaluation on low-index nonpolar surfaces
Comparison of defect energetics under different oxygen chemical potentials
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a band gap exceeding 3 eV, shallow-donor behavior for several impurities, and work functions up to ~8 eV depending on surface termination and defect configuration.
watch_item: Performance may be reduced if oxygen chemical potential is not tightly controlled, since ordered surface O vacancies are favored and can lower the work function.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
